name: Ethoheptazine
summary: Ethoheptazine (trade name Zactane) is an opioid analgesic from the phenazepane family. It was invented in the 1950s and is a ring expanded analogue of pethidine.

pharmacology.text: Ethoheptazine produces similar effects to other opioids, including analgesia, sedation, dizziness, and nausea.

uses.text: It was sold by itself as Zactane, and is still available as a combination product with acetylsalicylic acid and meprobamate as Equagesic, which is used for the treatment of conditions where both pain and anxiety are present. It was also investigated for use as an antitussive. It is no longer prescribed, as it is no longer FDA approved, and not available for United States' Pharmacy Processing.
